subject: Maths
atp_edition: undated (DBE Grade R Resource Kit 'Laying Solid Foundations for Learning')
basis: DBE Grade R Resource Kit lesson plans (no ATP published)

terms.theme: My body; My senses; My family; Keeping clean and fit; Healthy eating

topics.name: My body: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 5 and more; counts counters in the hand
Number 1: recognises, names and writes the numeral 1 and number word 'one'
Introduced to the circle
Names 'one more' and 'one less'
Compares and orders objects by length and height using vocabulary (tall, short, longer, shorter); height chart of the class
Copies pegboard patterns

topics.name: My senses: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 5 and more
Number 2: numeral, number word 'two' and pegboard pattern
Introduced to the square (sides and corners)
Sorts objects into groups of two
Creates and continues patterns (two and three colours)
Describes and compares objects by mass: heavy, heavier, light, lighter

topics.name: My family: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 5 and more; counting to 10 warm-up
Number 3: numeral and number word 'three'; groups of three
Introduced to the triangle
Answers verbal addition and subtraction problems with solutions to 4
Sorts objects according to size
Collects and sorts objects and displays them as a pictograph

topics.name: Keeping clean and fit: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 5 and more
Number 4: numeral and number word 'four'; things that come in fours
Introduced to the rectangle and how it differs from other shapes
Builds up and breaks down numbers to 4 using counters
Oral addition and subtraction word sums (e.g. I have four buttons, I drop two)

topics.name: Healthy eating: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 5 and more (counting up to six straws)
Revises numbers 1 to 3 and number words one to three
Introduced to the heart shape
Copies and extends simple patterns using concrete objects and drawings
Follows instructions and directions
Collects data (food pictures) and sorts food into groups
Oral addition and subtraction problems using straws as counters

sba: Numeracy assessment (weeks 1-2): count five counters; identify, write and make the number 1; find single items in the classroom (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 3-4): continue a two-colour pattern, create a three-colour pattern, sort counters and explain (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 5-6): name, describe and draw circle, square and triangle; draw bigger and smaller shapes (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 7-8): count out four of six counters; count varied items; verbal addition and subtraction (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 9-10): count six straws; addition and subtraction with straws; form circle, square, triangle and rectangle with straws (checklist)

terms.theme: Friends; This is what I wear; Shapes and colours in my community; Opposites; Gardens and bugs

topics.name: Friends: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10; estimates a quantity and checks by counting
Revises numbers 1 to 4; matches numerals, number words and dot patterns
Introduced to the diamond shape (sides and corners)
Concepts of more, less and equal
Solves and explains practical problems involving equal sharing and grouping of at least 6, including remainders
Sorts fruit in various ways (colour, size, type)

topics.name: This is what I wear: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10
Number 5: numeral and number word 'five'
Introduced to the oval shape
Equal sharing and grouping to 6; counting pairs (socks)
Compares and orders objects by length using vocabulary (long, longer, short, shorter)
Oral addition and subtraction problems; sequencing clothes on a washing line

topics.name: Shapes and colours in my community: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10
Number 6: numeral and number word 'six'
Revises all shapes and colours; sorts shapes by criteria (sides, round, flat)
Creates and completes simple patterns with shapes
Solves orally stated addition and subtraction problems up to 6
Collects and sorts data: graphs shapes by shape, colour and size

topics.name: Opposites: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10
Revises numbers 1 to 6 and number words one to six
Revises all shapes and colours
Breaks up 6 into two groups and explains own groupings; sorts objects by own criteria
Solves oral addition and subtraction problems with solutions to at least 6 and explains own solutions

topics.name: Gardens and bugs: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10; counts legs and groups of 2 and 3 on bugs
Revises numbers 1 to 6 and number words one to six; matches number, word and dots on a die
Revises all shapes and colours; designs bugs from shapes
Solves oral addition and subtraction problems with solutions to at least 6 using concrete apparatus or drawings
Makes bug counting books with number and number word on each page

sba: Numeracy assessment (weeks 11-12): order and match numerals, number words and dots 1-4; write a number and draw matching items (checklist and holistic rubric)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 13-14): count socks, pair them and count pairs; describe socks by length (holistic rubric)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 15-16): sort shapes and explain; continue and create shape patterns; make a picture from shapes (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 17-18): count out 6 of 10 counters; break 6 into two groups and explain (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 19-20): throw a die, match number word and count toothpick legs onto ladybugs; solve problems with apparatus (checklist)

terms.theme: Time and weather; Keeping safe; The sky (day and night); People who help us; Helping hands

topics.name: Time and weather: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts objects in the story Clouds
Sorts cloud pictures by size (length) and sequences them from biggest to smallest
Describes morning, afternoon and night
Describes the mass of water-filled bags or tins: heavy, light, heaviest, lightest
Collects, represents and analyses data (what learners are wearing) as a pictograph (Worksheet 4)
Uses mathematical language (big, small, more than, less than)

topics.name: Keeping safe: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts items and tells how many altogether
Manipulates household containers and sorts them into those that slide and those that roll
Describes properties of objects that roll (round edges) and slide (flat sides)
Identifies boxes among 3-D objects and describes their properties
Sorts cutlery and containers by own criteria (safe/not safe, shape, size, colour)

topics.name: The sky (day and night): Numeracy
subtopics: Counts objects to 10 (owls' wings, beaks, claws)
Verbal subtraction with apparatus and re-counting; shows answers with number cards
Recognises numerals 1 to 10
Responds to positional language (on, next to, behind, in front of, under)
Crescent shape; identifies shapes in a picture (Worksheet 4); copies shape patterns on pegboards

topics.name: People who help us: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10; identifies numerals and number words to 6
Shares concrete apparatus to find leftovers (odd) or no leftovers (even), to at least 6
Uses concrete apparatus to subtract from at least 6
Shares pizzas/cakes cut into 2 to 6 slices between plates
Explains solutions to problems

topics.name: Helping hands: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts to 10
Breaks down and builds up numbers to 8; matches numeral and word cards to 8
Solves verbally stated addition and subtraction story sums in the range 1-8 with counters
Adds and subtracts dice numbers with counters (money box coins)
Uses mathematical language to express problem-solving strategies

sba: Numeracy assessment (weeks 21-22): count three tins, order biggest to smallest and heaviest to lightest (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 23-24): count containers; identify items that roll and slide and explain; identify boxes (checklist)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 25-26): count logi-shape houses and parts, subtract and show numeral cards (checklist); positional language with a chair (observation)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 27-28): count 10 buttons and match numeral and word; take away from six; share paper pizzas and predict leftovers (holistic rubric)
Numeracy assessment (weeks 29-30): count 10 counters; bottle-top number bonds to 8 with numeral and word cards; story sums to 8 (checklist)

terms.theme: New life; This is where people live

topics.name: New life: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts objects to 10
Investigates symmetry in nature using mirrors; completes an incomplete symmetrical picture on pegboards
Compares the length of objects concretely and sorts from longest to shortest (caterpillars, tubes)
Creates own patterns; copies pegboard patterns
Counts legs of plasticine animals; older and younger

topics.name: This is where people live: Numeracy
subtopics: Counts buildings, windows, doors and tiles on Poster 17
Symmetry: pegboard block houses symmetrical on both sides
Shape puzzles; covers a square floor area with shape cut-outs
Theme-related subtraction story sums with 10 counters (e.g. Bob has 8 nails, hammers 4)
Discusses tools and materials used for building a house

sba: Numeracy assessment (weeks 31-32): count 10 counters; order tubes by length; complete half a pegboard pattern symmetrically (checklist)
